questions.question: You are on a budget and payday is another week away for you. But you’re really craving food from your favorite restaurant, so you decide to treat yourself. When you get the check, what do you do?
options: Don’t leave a tip. You’re broke and they probably get enough tips from other customers.
Leave a dollar. It’s not much but at least you tipped!
Leave a 20% tip. If you decide to go out to eat, you need to leave a fair tip.
questions.answer: Leave a 20% tip. If you decide to go out to eat, you need to leave a fair tip.

questions.question: Your coworker forgot to log out of their email account on a shared computer. You see a few unread messages from the manager. What do you do?
options: Ignore it and log them out immediately.
Take a quick peek — it’s probably harmless curiosity.
Forward one to yourself to see what the manager says about the team.
questions.answer: Ignore it and log them out immediately.

questions.question: You find a wallet on the street with cash and an ID inside. What’s your move?
options: Take the cash and drop the wallet in a mailbox.
Leave it there; someone else will deal with it.
Return it intact to the owner or local authorities.
questions.answer: Return it intact to the owner or local authorities.

questions.question: You’re working remotely and no one is monitoring your hours. You’ve finished your work early. What do you do?
options: Clock out honestly and enjoy your free time.
Keep the timer running and get paid for the full hours.
Do extra work to impress your boss even if it’s unnecessary.
questions.answer: Clock out honestly and enjoy your free time.

questions.question: You accidentally receive confidential data from another department that you weren’t supposed to see. What’s the ethical action?
options: Delete it and inform the sender immediately.
Keep a copy — it might be useful later.
Do nothing. If they sent it, it’s their problem.
questions.answer: Delete it and inform the sender immediately.

questions.question: A friend asks you to help them cheat on an online exam by feeding them answers. What do you do?
options: Help them — it’s just one test.
Refuse politely and encourage them to study.
Give them partial answers so it’s not too obvious.
questions.answer: Refuse politely and encourage them to study.

questions.question: You’re returning an item online and accidentally receive a refund *and* the product. What’s the right thing to do?
options: Keep both — it’s their mistake.
Notify the company and offer to return or repay.
Wait to see if they contact you first.
questions.answer: Notify the company and offer to return or repay.

questions.question: You see a coworker taking credit for your idea in a meeting. What’s the ethical response?
options: Call them out aggressively during the meeting.
Stay calm and talk to them or your manager privately afterward.
Do nothing — confrontation isn’t worth it.
questions.answer: Stay calm and talk to them or your manager privately afterward.

questions.question: You’re writing a report and tempted to copy text from an article online without citing it. What should you do?
options: Reword it in your own language and cite the source.
Copy it as-is — no one will notice.
Delete the paragraph entirely; it’s too much work.
questions.answer: Reword it in your own language and cite the source.

questions.question: You accidentally overhear private information about layoffs at work. A coworker asks you if you know anything. What do you do?
options: Tell them what you heard — they deserve to know.
Say you’re not sure and change the subject.
Speculate openly with others to see what they’ve heard.
questions.answer: Say you’re not sure and change the subject.
